title: Big super 'must unite' on cybersecurity
full_text:
The Albanese government has repeatedly told the superannuation industry to stop arguing and work together to bolster defences against cybersecurity threats amid fears the sector is reacting too slowly and splintering, leaving members exposed just a year after a major co-ordinated attack on funds.
Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino went as far as to urge the Association of Super Funds of Australia and Financial Services Council - two of the retirement savings sector's three lobby groups - to combine their work as soon as possible to address lingering "concerns that Treasury and the regulators [have] about the level of cyber resilience" at the big funds.
"The government sees value in promoting a more unified and co-ordinated industry response to cyber risks," he wrote to the chairs of the lobby groups in a February letter obtained by The Australian Financial Review. "Multiple approaches to addressing this issue have the potential to create unnecessary uncertainty in response to an incident, which would be undesirable."
